question:
A 17-year-old female is brought to the pediatrician by her father due to concerns about delayed
puberty, as she has not yet developed while her peers have. The patient reports feeling well with no
specific complaints. Her vital signs include a temperature of 98.9°F, heart rate of 71 beats per minute,
and blood pressure of 143/97 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals undeveloped breasts, normal
external and internal female genitalia, and Tanner stage I development. Her body mass index is
normal, she is in the 40th percentile for height, and she is cooperative and pleasant during the
interview. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Low serum cortisol (B) XY karyotype (C) Growth hormone deficiency (D) Elevated FSH levels (E) Low
serum aldosterone (F) Hypokalemia (G) Primary hypothyroidism (H) Hyperandrogenism (I) Turner
syndrome karyotype (J) Aromatase enzyme deficiency
 A. Low serum cortisol
B. Hyperandrogenism
C. Turner syndrome karyotype
D. Growth hormone deficiency
E. Primary hypothyroidism
F. Aromatase enzyme deficiency
G. XY karyotype
H. Hypokalemia
I. Low serum aldosterone
J. Elevated FSH levels
